part: §59–§75 · Curses on whoever erases the name

sentences.l: But rules as king, if anyone,
sentences.i: But if anyone rules as king,
sentences.n: The curses begin. From here to the end the inscription is one long condition (§59–§72), then the curse (§73) and the wish that the name endure (§74–§75). The verb comes first: hantawattatti 'rules as king' is the present 3rd singular (-tti, written ti-i) of hantawatta- 'exercise kingship', a verb made on the word for 'king' and written with the same REX sign, ta re-sounding the stem. It carries =pa, the topic shifter (written pa, transcribed =ba by the corpus) that turns from the blessings of §49–§58 to this new subject, and =wa. kwari 'if' is a single ligature, kwa/i+ra/i. The subject stands last: kwis-ha 'anyone' is the pronoun kwi- (the relative 'who' of §26–§27) in the common nominative -s, made indefinite by the suffix -ha, 'any-'. A register break follows the clause.

morph.gloss: rule as king, exercise kingship (REX, the king sign, with ta for the stem)
3rd person singular present — 'rules as king' (written ti-i)

sentences.n: niba 'or' (written ní-pa) opens the clause and carries =wa and =as 'he', the clitic pronoun in the nominative — the 'anyone' of §59. There is no verb: Luwian can set two nominatives side by side, 'he (is) …'. CAPUT-ttis is the head sign CAPUT with ti and the nominative -s, as in §34; the corpus glosses the word '(noble)man' and leaves its Luwian form open, so the logogram is not voiced. Set beside the king of §59, the higher sense 'nobleman' seems meant, but that is read from the pairing, not settled by the word. Before CAPUT stands the small marker the script sets before personal names (shown, not read). The clause begins a new line, since §59 ends with a register break.

morph.gloss: (noble)man, person (written with the head sign CAPUT; the corpus leaves the Luwian word open)

sentences.n: A long clitic chain on the first word. CAPUT-ttiyanza is an adjective made from CAPUT-tt(i)- with -iya-, '(noble)man's, of a (noble)man', in the neuter nominative singular (-nza), agreeing with alamanza 'name' (alaman-, neuter nominative singular). On it hang =ha 'and', =wa, =du 'to him' (the clitic pronoun in the dative, as in §39) and =tta, the place particle, left untranslated. 'To him (is) a name' is how Luwian says 'he has a name'. What a nobleman's name implies (a title, a rank) the clause does not say. The personal-name marker stands before CAPUT again.

morph.gloss: neuter singular nominative ending, agreeing with 'name'

sentences.n: A short clause, and one without =wa. za 'this' is the demonstrative in the neuter accusative singular, and assazzaya 'proclaims, says' is the present 3rd singular of assazza- 'say, proclaim', the ending -i spelled -ia (as taya in §48); sa₅ is one of the several signs for sa. 'This' points forward: the words he says follow in §63–§64.

sentences.l: 'Away I delete Azatiwada's name from these gates,
sentences.i: 'I will erase Azatiwada's name from these gates
sentences.n: His words. ahha 'away' (ARHA, which the corpus sets in braces, as in §51) opens the clause and carries =wa and =tta; with the verb it makes 'delete away', that is, erase. iTiwi 'I delete' is the present 1st singular (-wi) of i(ya)Ti- 'delete', under a classifier known only by its list number, L69; the capital T marks a sound the spelling leaves open. The present stands for what he means to do, hence the English 'will'. A register break comes before Azzattiwadas(sa) 'of Azatiwada', a genitive whose full ending the corpus leaves open (-s(sa)), under LITUUS, the sign that stands before the ruler's name. alamanza 'name' is the neuter accusative singular, its la written with the other l-sign, lá/í. hilanari zin 'from these gates' are two instrumentals: hilan(a)- 'gate(s)', the gate sign PORTA with la and na re-sounding the stem and the ending -ari (-adi, the d sounded r), and za- 'this' (zi-na). The case means 'with, by'; 'from' is how it reads with 'erase'.

morph.gloss: away, back (ARHA; set in braces by the corpus) — with the verb, 'delete away, erase'
delete, erase (classified by the sign L69; the capital T marks a sound the spelling leaves open)
1st person singular present — 'I delete' (here of what he means to do)
genitive ending — 'of Azatiwada' (the corpus leaves the full ending open)
name (the la written with the l-sign lá/í)
instrumental ending — 'from' (-adi, the d sounded r)

sentences.l: and for myself my name into (them) I strike.'
sentences.i: and strike my own name into them.'
sentences.n: wa=mu=tta: =wa, then =mu 'me', a dative — 'for myself' — and the place particle. A register break comes before ammanza 'my' (ami(ya)-, neuter accusative singular -nza, agreeing with alamanza 'name'). anta 'in, into' goes with the verb: tubiwi 'I strike' is the present 1st singular (-wi) of tub(a)i- 'strike'. To strike a name into stone is to cut it with the chisel; '(them)', the gates, is supplied from §63.

morph.gloss: neuter singular accusative ending, agreeing with 'name'

sentences.n: niba=wa=as 'or he', as in §60, the pronoun here written sá. alunnazzaia 'covets' is the present 3rd singular (-i, spelled -ia) of alunnazza- 'covet'. Its classifier is the heart sign COR, which has no verifiable Unicode sign: it is shown with the ▢ placeholder, which here marks a gap in the sign repertoire, not damage to the stone. The verb takes the dative: harnissi zatti 'this fortress' (CASTRUM with ní and si, and za- 'this' with -tti, as in §40). After CASTRUM the corpus supplies a closing quotation mark (<”>); such marks are dropped here, so nothing editorial shows. A register break follows the clause.

morph.gloss: covet (classified by the heart sign COR, shown ▢: no verifiable sign)
dative singular ending (the si sign also carries the stem's s)
dative singular ending — 'this', with harnissi; covet takes the dative

sentences.n: wa=tta, then anta 'in' with tamari 'builds', the present 3rd singular of tama- 'build' (the verb of §38); the ending -ri (-di, the d sounded r) is written here with its i alone. The MI attached to AEDIFICARE is set in braces by the corpus, as throughout. hilana 'gates' (PORTA-la-na) and zaya 'these' are neuter plural accusatives, the object. To 'build in' gates is most naturally to wall them up, closing the way through; that is a reading of the phrase, not a certainty. The clause begins a new line.

morph.gloss: build (AEDIFICARE; its MI set in braces by the corpus)
3rd person singular present — 'builds' (-di sounded -ri; only the i written)
gate(s), gateway (PORTA, the gate sign) — neuter plural accusative

sentences.n: A relative clause hanging on the gates of §66, without =wa. kwaya 'which' is the relative kwi- in the neuter plural accusative (-ya), and Azzattiwadas, nominative -s under LITUUS, is its subject. izzira 'made' is the past 3rd singular of izzi(ya)- 'make' (the verb of §50): the ending -ta is sounded -ra and written with the l-sign lá/í.

morph.gloss: 3rd person singular past — 'made' (-ta sounded -ra, written with the l-sign lá/í)

sentences.n: a=wa, the plain connective with =wa. zari 'here' is zadi, the d sounded r (za with the ligature ri+i). assazzaya 'says, proclaims' as in §62. Whether 'here' means at this place (at the gates) or 'thereupon' cannot be decided from the word alone.

morph.gloss: here (sounded zari, the d heard as r)

sentences.i: 'I will make gates of my own
sentences.n: His second speech. warallaya 'own' is warall(a/i)- in the neuter plural accusative (-ya), agreeing with hilana 'gates'; it begins with the ligature wa/i+ra/i, here simply war-, and carries =wa. izziwi 'I make' is izzi(ya)- in the present 1st singular (-wi), with the sense of what he intends, as in §63. 'Own' refers to the speaker: the gates are to become his, whether by rebuilding them or only by claiming them, the clause does not say.

morph.gloss: neuter plural accusative ending, agreeing with 'gates'
gate(s), gateway (PORTA, the gate sign) — neuter plural accusative

sentences.l: and my name for myself into (them) I strike.'
sentences.i: and strike my own name into them.'
sentences.n: §64 again, nearly to the letter, now with =ha 'and' in the chain: ammanza=ha=wa=mu=tta 'and my … for myself (into)'. In ammanza the corpus prints z<a>: the a of the za sign is its editorial completion; the sign is shown as za. alamanza ends in an extra a that spells out the final vowel. anta tubiwi 'into … I strike', as in §64.

morph.gloss: neuter singular accusative ending (the corpus supplies the a of za: z<a>)
neuter singular accusative ending (the a spells out the vowel)

sentences.i: or walls them up out of covetousness,
sentences.n: Another alternative. ni 'or' (so the corpus glosses it, as it does niba) with =wa and =tta. alunnammadi is an instrumental (-adi, written ti) of alunnamm(a)- 'lust', the noun belonging with alunnazza- 'covet' of §65 and, like it, under the heart sign COR (▢: no verifiable sign). 'With lust' is the case's plain sense; the English says 'out of covetousness' to keep the link to §65 and avoid the wrong kind of lust. anta tamari 'builds in' as in §66, with no object written; the verb is spelled AEDIFICARE.MI (the MI in braces) with ri+i and i. A register break closes the clause.

morph.gloss: lust, covetousness (classified by the heart sign COR, shown ▢: no verifiable sign)
build (AEDIFICARE.MI; its MI set in braces by the corpus)

sentences.n: The corpus divides §72 into two clauses, 72a and 72b; both carry the number 72 here. 72a has no verb of its own: niba=wa 'or', and attuwalastarrari, the instrumental (-ari: -adi, the d sounded r) of attuwalastr(i)- 'viciousness', an abstract noun (suffix -astarr-) on attuwal- 'bad', whose logogram MALUS begins the word, followed by la/i for the end of the stem. The verb it waits for is the 'builds in' of 72b. It begins a new line, and a register break follows.

morph.gloss: viciousness — an abstract noun on attuwal- 'bad' (MALUS)
instrumental ending — 'with, out of' (-adi, the d sounded r)

sentences.l: or with badness in (he) builds these gates,
sentences.i: or out of wickedness walls up these gates —
sentences.n: The last alternative, with the verb and object 72a lacks. niba=wa 'or' (ní-i-pa, the i spelling out the vowel). haniyattastarradi is a second abstract noun of the same build (-astarr-, instrumental -adi), glossed 'badness' by the corpus; it is spelled out in syllables under MALUS₂, a second 'bad' sign, as classifier. 'Viciousness' and 'wickedness' only mark that two different words stand here; how they differ is not known. anta tamari zaya hilana 'builds in these gates' takes up §66. In AEDIFICARE+MI the corpus sets the MI in braces and flags it ^!, noting an irregularity in the sign as carved; it is shown in its regular form.

morph.gloss: or (the i spells out the vowel)
badness, wickedness — an abstract noun (classified by MALUS₂, a 'bad' sign)
build (AEDIFICARE+MI; the MI set in braces and flagged ^! by the corpus)
gate(s), gateway (PORTA, the gate sign) — neuter plural accusative

sentences.l: Away may delete — Tarhunzas of heaven, Tiwazas of heaven, Iyas and all the gods — that kingdom, and that king, and that (noble)man.
sentences.i: then may Tarhunzas of heaven, Tiwazas of heaven, Iyas and all the gods erase that kingdom, and that king, and that nobleman.
sentences.n: The penalty. Nothing marks it as the 'then' (supplied in the English) except the change of mood, to the imperative: wa=tta, then after a register break ahha 'away' (ARHA, in braces) and iyaTintu 'may they delete', the 3rd plural imperative (-ntu, the n unwritten) of the verb of §63, here with the hand sign MANUS as classifier — the one who would erase the name is himself to be erased. The subjects are nominatives. tippasassis 'of heaven', written with the sky sign CAELUM alone, is a possessive adjective (-assi-, nominative -s) from tippas- 'sky'; it stands before Tarhunzas and again before Tiwazas, the Sun-god (SOL, the sun sign, with za-sá): the stem Tiwad- with its d sounded z before the nominative -s, as Tarhunt- gives Tarhunzas; the name is given in that form here and in §75. Then Iyas, written in syllables (i-ia-sá), the god the corpus identifies with Ea; and taniminzi=ha massaninzi 'and all the gods' (OMNIS.MI and DEUS, nominative plural -nzi). DEUS stands before each name as classifier. The objects are three accusatives with aba- 'that': aba hantawattahisa 'that kingdom' (REX with hi and the neuter ending -sa: hantawattahi(d)- 'kingship, kingdom'), aban=ha hantawattin 'and that king' (aban spelled á-pa, its n unwritten; REX-na), aban=ha=wa CAPUT-ttin 'and that (noble)man' (CAPUT-ti-na, accusative -n), with =wa coming late in the clause. King and (noble)man answer §59–§60; the kingdom is added.

morph.gloss: away, back (ARHA; set in braces by the corpus) — with the verb, 'delete away, erase'
delete, erase (classified by the hand sign MANUS; the capital T marks a sound the spelling leaves open)
3rd person plural imperative — 'may they delete' (the n unwritten)
sky, heaven — here its possessive adjective tippasassis 'of heaven' (written with the sky sign CAELUM alone) — nominative singular, with Tarhunzas
sky, heaven — here its possessive adjective tippasassis 'of heaven' (written with the sky sign CAELUM alone) — nominative singular, with Tiwazas
the Sun-god, named Tiwazas here (written with the sun sign SOL) — the d sounded z before the ending
Iyas, a god (DN) — the corpus identifies him with Ea
kingship, kingdom (REX, with the abstract suffix -hi(d)-)
that (demonstrative) — common accusative singular aban (the n unwritten)
that (demonstrative) — common accusative singular aban (the n unwritten)
(noble)man, person (written with the head sign CAPUT; the corpus leaves the Luwian word open)

sentences.l: Afterwards away(?) may stay, for all times, Azatiwada's name,
sentences.i: And afterwards may Azatiwada's name remain for all times,
sentences.n: appan=wa 'afterwards' (POST-na, the 'behind' of §40, here of time). ahha 'away' (ARHA, in braces) is followed in the corpus by ?!, which flags the sign as irregular and its reading as uncertain; with tazzattu its force is unclear: the literal line queries it, and the English leaves it out. tazzattu 'may it stay' is the 3rd singular imperative (-ttu) of tazza- 'stay', under the leg sign CRUS as classifier, after which the corpus supplies a closing quotation mark (<”>: editorial, not shown). arinzi taniminzi 'all times' are common plural accusatives of extent: ar(i)- 'time', with the syllabogram ara/i (one of two signs with that value), and OMNIS.MI-zi. The subject comes last: Azzattiwadas(sa) alamanza 'Azatiwada's name' — the genitive, here under the eye sign OCULUS as classifier where §63 and §67 have LITUUS, and alamanza, neuter nominative singular.

morph.gloss: away, back (ARHA; set in braces and flagged ?! by the corpus) — its force here unclear
stay, remain (classified by the leg sign CRUS)
genitive ending — 'of Azatiwada' (the corpus leaves the full ending open)
name (the la written with the l-sign lá/í) — the subject

sentences.l: of Armas and of Tiwazas when the name stands.
sentences.i: as long as the name of Armas and of Tiwazas stands.
sentences.n: Two divine genitives open the clause: Armas(sa)=wa 'of Armas', the Moon-god, written with the moon sign LUNA (its MI in braces) and sa, carrying =wa; and Tiwadas(sa)=ha 'and of Tiwazas' (the corpus's transcription; the name as in §73), the sun sign SOL with =ha, its genitive ending not written at all. Both stand under DEUS. kwari is the 'if' of §59, here spelled kwa/i-ri+i. With tai 'stands' (the present 3rd singular of ta- 'stand', §48, written with the leg sign CRUS as logogram), 'if' gives an odd sense; this edition reads it as 'when', shading into 'as long as'. That is an interpretation, not the corpus's gloss, which is 'if' only: Azatiwada's name is to last while the name of the moon and the sun lasts. alamanza 'name' is the subject, neuter nominative singular, and the genitives depend on it.

morph.gloss: Armas, the Moon-god (written with the moon sign LUNA, its MI set in braces by the corpus)
genitive ending — 'of Armas' (the corpus leaves the full ending open)
the Sun-god, Tiwazas (written with the sun sign SOL) — genitive, 'of Tiwazas', its ending unwritten
if (so the corpus) — here read 'when, as long as'
